prompt:
You are a grounded brand-outreach assistant for our team. Use only the evidence passages below.
Never use outside knowledge. Return valid JSON only.

Separate three things:
1. OBSERVED FACTS - things a passage actually states about this company. Each fact is a claim with an id (C1, C2, ...),
   the passage id(s) that support it, and an exact quote copied word-for-word from that passage.
2. UNKNOWNS - things the evidence does not tell us (put them in "unknowns"). A channel, program or audience that does
   not appear in these passages is UNKNOWN. It is never a weakness, never a "gap", and never a reason for outreach.
3. PROPOSALS - collaboration ideas from our team. Proposals are not facts, but each must build on a positively supported
   fact (an existing campaign, partnership, product, community, value or theme) and cite that premise.

Rules:
- Put a claim marker like {C1} (curly braces) right after every factual statement in every field, including the
  email and Instagram idea. Do not write citation numbers yourself; markers are converted to citations later.
- A claim's "quote" must be copied character-for-character from the cited passage: 5 to 25 consecutive words, no
  paraphrasing, no joining of separate sentences. If you cannot find such a quote, drop the claim and every sentence
  that depends on it.
- Audience and strategy sentences are factual: each needs a marker. If no passage states the audience, write
  INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE instead of guessing.
- Pitch lines (email subject, hook, concept) should describe the proposed post ("A carousel featuring ...",
  "Collaborate on ..."). Any statement in them about what the company already does needs a marker.
- Respect passage types. "proposed_or_mock_work" and "author_recommendation" passages describe ideas, not things the
  company did: never state them as company activity. "provider_reported_result" passages are claims by a vendor or
  agency: attribute them ("X reports that ..."). "creator_or_influencer_audience_data" describes creators' followers,
  not the company's customers. "vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics" passages are a tool vendor's estimates
  (e.g. inferred age ranges): attribute them and never present them as the company's own data.
  "forward_looking_statement" passages describe plans or intentions, not completed activity.
- Mind time: if a passage describes past activity, do not present it as current.
- "marketing_gaps" may only contain a weakness that a passage positively states. Usually it is [].
- Never promise results. Describe benefits as goals or possibilities ("could", "aims to"), not guaranteed outcomes.
- Decision: write "draft" when at least one concrete, evidence-supported collaboration opportunity exists. Otherwise write
  "abstain", give an abstain_reason, set pitch fields to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and leave collaboration_opportunities empty.
- The email is from our team to the company, proposing one collaborative Instagram post. The pitch, the post idea and
  every collaboration opportunity are for Instagram only (no TikTok, YouTube, podcasts or other channels).
- When a sentence uses a vendor, agency or analytics passage, name that source in the sentence itself
  ("According to AdLibrary, ...", "Attentive reports that ...").
- Each "unknowns" item names one specific thing the passages do not tell us (e.g. "Whether X runs a creator program").
  Never write placeholder text such as "what the evidence does not show".

Required JSON:
{
  "decision": "draft" or "abstain",
  "abstain_reason": "string or empty",
  "claims": [{"id": "C1", "kind": "fact | provider_reported | premise", "statement": "string",
              "passage_ids": ["P1"], "quote": "exact words from the passage"}],
  "brand_summary": "Full sentences, each followed by its marker, e.g. "X makes ... {C1}." Never only markers. Or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "likely_target_audience": "A full sentence followed by its marker, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "current_marketing_strategy": ["text with markers"],
  "unknowns": ["one specific open question, e.g. Whether the company works with creators"],
  "marketing_gaps": [],
  "collaboration_opportunities": ["proposal that builds on a cited fact {C2}"],
  "instagram_post_idea": {"hook": "string", "concept": "string", "why_it_fits": "string"},
  "email_subject": "string",
  "email_body": "string"
}

Company: Branch Furniture (company_id branch-furniture; category: office furniture)
Official domains: branchfurniture.com, branchfurniture.ca
Recipient: the marketing team
Packet status: ok

Evidence passages:
[P1] source: https://www.branchfurniture.com/pages/industrious-case-study | document: official_domain | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"The Outcome A scalable furnishing program that enabled faster location launches and expansions with durable, design-forward furniture aligned to brand standards and operational needs."

[P2] source: https://www.branchfurniture.com/pages/industrious-case-study | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"The Impact Opening delays tied to furnishing and fit-out timelines created operational pressure and risked slowing revenue ramp. Industrious needed a partner that could deliver at speed, at scale, and with consistent quality across markets. Our approach focused on creating standardized yet flexible furniture packages that could adapt to different floor plans and member needs while preserving a cohesive brand experience. Rather than one rigid template, the furnishing strategy allowed for modular layouts across private offices, shared work areas, and collaboration zones."

[P3] source: https://www.branchfurniture.com/pages/projects | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Venture Capital & Private Equity Digital Marketing #### Furnishing a spacious, collaborative digital marketing space Headcount: 75 Boise Real Estate"

[P4] source: https://www.branchfurniture.com/pages/design-values | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Sustainable Furniture that supports you and the world We strive to incorporate sustainable principles into our product life cycle, and offset in areas where we can’t. How We Do It: Our products are built for durability and repairability to provide a long and productive life. Our Flex program lets corporate customers return furniture for a second use. We offset shipping emissions, and work with the Arbor Day Foundation to plant trees each holiday season. We're actively exploring improvements in our single-use packaging and more circularity across our supply chain. We've planted over 100,000 trees to date"

[P5] source: https://www.branchfurniture.com/pages/industrious-case-study | document: official_domain | type: historical_activity | dates in text: 2024, 2025 | published: unknown
"Branch furniture has now been deployed across multiple Industrious locations, supporting new site launches and expansions throughout 2024–2025."

[P6] source: https://www.branchfurniture.com/pages/design-values | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Flexible Your workspace should adapt to your needs Whether you're furnishing a home office in a studio or a growing team office in a commercial building, our products are designed to work together and change with you. How We Do It: We use consistent sizes and materials across our products to support endless configurations. Product assembly is a breeze, and we offer many corporate customers the ability to trade-in current Branch furniture as needs change. Our Verve Chair takes 20 minutes to assemble"

[P7] source: https://www.branchfurniture.com/pages/about-us | document: official_domain | type: brand_positioning | dates in text: 2018 | published: unknown
"Sale Shop By Office Chairs Desks & Tables Bundles Storage & Accessories Lounge Black Friday Explore Seating Desks & Tables Breakout & Meeting Storage & Accessories Sale Country Flag ABOUT US At Branch, we make it easy for people and teams to build a beautiful workspace where you can feel and work your best. OUR STORY In 2018, our CEO Greg Hayes discovered a problem—buying office furniture is a tremendous hassle. After furnishing dozens of offices for a commercial real estate startup, Greg realized the average office furniture company falls into one of two categories: high quality, but expensive and slow, or affordable and fast but lacking in quality and service."

[P8] source: https://www.branchfurniture.com/pages/about-us | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Verified Customer I've had my Branch Office Desk now for a couple of weeks and absolutely LOVE everything about it...Hands down one the of the best purchases I've made and I'm now a HUGE fan of Branch. ★★★★★ John B. Verified Customer The collaboration and flexibility on Branch’s part to deliver on their promise was impressive, and it’s why we’d be happy to work with them again in the future as we expand our headcount. ★★★★★ Jovanna F. Verified Customer Great communication throughout the process, paired with easy delivery and assembly. We'll be ordering additional office furniture soon. ★★★★★ Brenden C. Verified Customer see reviews OUR COMMITMENT We care about how the world works."

[P9] source: https://www.branchfurniture.com/pages/about-us | document: official_domain | type: brand_positioning | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Sustainability We make furniture that’s easily serviceable, made out of recycled (and recyclable) materials, and can be traded in as your team grows. Responsibility Every year, we set aside a portion of our revenue to donate to charitable organizations that share our ambition of making work better for everyone. BACKED BY THE BEST GET IN TOUCH We’d love to hear from you, whether you’re looking to join our team, partner with us, or just say hello. Send us a note and we’ll get in touch."

[P10] source: https://www.branchfurniture.com/pages/projects | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"× Visit our Branch Furniture Partner Location in New York to try out a selection of our products in person. Visit our Partner Page to see what's in stock."
